question: Who was declared the Emperor of India by the revolting sepoys during the 1857 uprising?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bahadur Shah II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bahadur Shah II**, also known as **Bahadur Shah Zafar**, was the last Mughal Emperor of India.
 
• He was declared the **Emperor of India** by the revolting sepoys during the **1857 uprising**, also known as the **First War of Independence**.
 
• The sepoys rallied around him as a symbolic figure to unite against British rule.
 
• Though he lacked military or administrative strength, his name was used to legitimize the rebellion.
 
• Bahadur Shah II was a **poet and philosopher**, and his reign marked the end of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• After the suppression of the revolt, he was captured by the British, tried, and exiled to **Rangoon (modern-day Yangon, Myanmar)**, where he died in 1862.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akbar II**__

 __
 
• Akbar II was the **second-to-last Mughal Emperor of India**, ruling from 1806 to 1837.
 
• He was the father of Bahadur Shah II and was more of a titular ruler under British domination.
 
• Akbar II is known for giving the title of **Raja** to **Rammohan Roy**, a prominent social reformer.
 
 
 
• **Shah Alam II**__
 __
 
• Shah Alam II ruled as the Mughal Emperor from **1760 to 1806**.
 
• He faced multiple invasions and political instability during his reign.
 
• He signed the **Treaty of Allahabad** with the British in 1765, which marked the beginning of British dominance in India.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb**__
 
 
• Aurangzeb was the **sixth Mughal Emperor**, ruling from 1658 to 1707.
 
• He expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest extent during his reign.
 
• Aurangzeb is known for his strict adherence to Islamic principles and policies of religious intolerance.
 
• His reign is considered the beginning of the decline of the Mughal Empire due to internal rebellions and administrative challenges.
